previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent pulmonary emboli on anticoagulation, chronic microcytic anemia, and costochondritis was admitted for acute worsening of chronic left-sided chest pain. Evaluation revealed no cardiac ischemia, pulmonary embolism, or other acute cardiopulmonary pathology. The chest pain was reproducible on palpation, consistent with musculoskeletal etiology. A urinary tract infection was identified on urinalysis and treated with a single dose of antibiotics. Dyspnea resolved without supplemental oxygen, and the patient remained hemodynamically stable. A posterior neck soft tissue swelling was noted, previously diagnosed as a lipoma, to be followed up outpatient. She was discharged home with continued home medications and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing management.
problems: Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen

Brief Hospital Course:
HOSPITAL COURSE: Ms. ___ is a ___ year old ___ 
woman with PMH of DVT/PE on ___ transferred from clinic to 
___ after been having found to have supratherapeutic INR of 8.7 
and anemia w/Hgb of 6 raising concern for GIB. In the ___, she 
received IV vitamin K, with reversal of INR to 1.3, and 1 unit 
pRBCs, with stable H/H of ___ at the time of discharge. She 
denied GIB and had no signs of bleeding on exam; was 
hemodynamically stable; and discharged with PCP, ___ 
clinic, and hematology follow up.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Anemia - While initially there was concern for acute blood 
loss and GIB in the setting of supratheraputic INR and anemia, 
as well as her history of gastritis and diverticulosis, she 
denied hematemesis, hematochezia, melena and had no evidence of 
active bleeding on exam (rectal exam w/brown stool). She was 
hemodynamically stable. She was transfused 1u pRBC, with 2PIVs 
in place, and IV PPI was given. After the transfusion she had an 
improvement more than would be expected (hgb 6 to 8), which was 
stable on recheck. No e/o hemolysis on labs. She has chronic 
microcytic anemia; iron deficiency could be considered as she 
states she does not always take her iron supplements. 

# Supratherapeutic INR - Likely ___ coumadin 2mg daily. Unclear 
why she became supratheraputic. Denies any new medication 
exposures to influence metabolism; however, review of OMR is 
notable for a prednisone taper (she was treated for suspected 
GCA in the setting of headaches/vision loss, with neg temporal 
artery biopsy) as well as corticosteroid injections in her back 
and costochondral joint in ___. In the setting of possible 
bleeding, was given 10 IV VitK in ___. Her warfarin dose was 
reduced from 2 mg to 1 mg daily and she was prescribed 
enoxaparin for bridging therapy. She had follow up with primary 
care and was instructed to follow up at ___ clinic as well 
at the time of discharge.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# HTN - Held home metoprolol in setting of concern for GIB, but 
home meds continued on discharge.
# dCHF - chronic, no signs of exacerbation currently. Diuretics 
held until acute GIB was ruled out, but home meds continued on 
discharge.
#Headache previously concerning for GCA, s/p negative temporal 
artery biopsy, on steroid taper: her home dose of prednisone was 
continued.
